candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a least common denominator and rewrite fraction parts as equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S01, and C.S01 all describe creating equivalent fractions with a shared denominator prior to subtraction for unlike denominators.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a mixed number with an improper fractional part into an equivalent standard mixed number before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include normalization of mixed numbers with improper fractional parts; A.S02 is broader, but its mixed-number normalization component aligns directly with B.S02 and C.S02.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number as a whole part plus a zero fraction with the needed denominator so it can be subtracted alongside a fraction or mixed number.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S03 and C.S03 match exactly as the explicit whole-number-to-n+0/d rewrite skill. A does not separate this from broader operand normalization and instead folds it into A.S02, so it is treated as a distinct concept only in B and C.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions once they share a denominator by subtracting numerators over the common denominator, including fraction parts within mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03 isolates fraction-part subtraction after denominator alignment. B and C do not separate this from whole-part subtraction, instead combining both under their broader aligned-subtraction skills.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number components of the quantities when working with mixed numbers or whole numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 isolates subtraction of whole-number parts. B.S04 and C.S04 combine whole-part and fraction-part subtraction into a single broader skill rather than treating whole-part subtraction separately.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator and/or subtract whole-number parts once the quantities are in compatible form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S04 and C.S04 are equivalent broad subtraction skills covering both fraction-part and whole-part subtraction after alignment. A splits this broader concept into A.S03 and A.S04, so no single A skill maps to this exact combined concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as an equivalent fraction unit and adjust the whole part when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S05, B.S05, and C.S05 all describe the same regrouping/borrowing operation from the whole part into the fractional part during subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms and express the final result in appropriate fraction, mixed-number, or integer form by combining whole and fractional parts when needed.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include the same end-of-problem skill: simplify the result and express it in final form.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks show strong agreement on common denominator finding, mixed-number normalization, borrowing/regrouping, and final simplification. The main structural difference is granularity: Expert A separates aligned subtraction into fraction-part and whole-part skills, while Experts B and C combine them into one broader subtraction skill. A second difference is that Experts B and C isolate rewriting a whole number as n + 0/d, whereas Expert A includes that operation inside a broader operand-normalization skill.
